v.rationale: All three pass their suites and share a sound design (Redis-backed onOneServer, ShouldBeUnique hourly job, Copenhagen timezone, batched cart deletes). The differences come from crash recovery. When I killed a sync job mid-run (lock left behind), impl-1 and impl-2 (UniqueFor 3600) dropped the next hourly dispatch. impl-3 (UniqueFor 3300) let it through. impl-1 and impl-3 also give their commands overlap locks with short expiries; I confirmed both locks can be taken again once expiry passes. impl-2 has no overlap lock, so nothing can get stuck. That is defensible, but its tests forbid overlap locks outright. impl-3 also has the strongest scheduler tests, including two schedule:run ticks in the same minute, and the most current conventions. It is ranked first. impl-1 is second: it has bounded overlap locks and a schedule:run test, but it has the dropped-hour bug, leaves the cache and queue on database instead of Redis in .env.example, and has a test that asserts nothing. impl-2 is third: it has the same dropped-hour bug and no end-to-end scheduler test, though its daylight-saving datasets and single-query batched delete are good. All three raise the shared Redis retry_after to suit one job.
